text: Kickoff: we're building a snake game in Python for the showcase on the 20th. Keep it dependency-free so anyone can run it.
Agreed on stdlib only. I'd use curses for rendering — it's in the standard library and gives us proper keyboard input.
curses doesn't work on Windows without a shim. Tom and I are both on Windows. Can we do a simple loop with a text grid instead?
Fair. Decision: plain text grid rendered to stdout, no curses. Input via a non-blocking read so it stays portable.
Recorded. Marcus takes the game loop and collision, Aisha takes rendering and the grid, Tom writes the tests. I'll review.
I'll aim for tests on collision and growth first — those are where the bugs live.
One more decision: the grid is 20x20 and the snake starts length 3 in the middle, moving right.
